//: The reviewed size of this package's surface: what a reader has to hold in
their head, counted the way `scripts/check-complexity.ts` counts it.
Limits are the exact current numbers, with no headroom on purpose. Byte
budgets carry ~1 % because compression is not byte-stable; a count is, and
headroom here would just be room to grow into without saying so. Raising a
number is a two-line change: the number, and why it moved.

publicDeclarations.why: Every exported name across all API reports. The number a consumer's editor offers them, and the number this package has to keep meaning something. 2026-09-06: +12 for the two zero-config setups — `withLivePreview()` for Next.js and the Nuxt module — which exist to remove lines from a consumer's project, not to add names to it. +5 for asset delivery: a route factory in each of the three adapters, plus what a route file re-exports in the two that name it. +13 for the build-time annotator, nine of them its own entry. 2026-09-06 (1.x-Upgrade): +3, the 1.x names 2.0 renamed rather than reshaped: `isPreviewRequest` on the two entries that exported it, and `PreviewSignal` back on `./astro`. Measured against the published 1.8.1 declarations entry by entry; everything whose meaning changed stays gone, because an alias there would type something the package no longer produces. 2026-09-06 (R9): −5, two concepts with no remaining reason — `PreviewBindingsCommonOptions`, a one-member base left behind when its sibling options type was removed in 2.0, and `AnnotatableEntry`, which had one member and one use.

entrySubpaths.why: Import specifiers in the manifest. Each one is a decision a reader makes before writing a line of code, so a new entry needs a reason a sentence can hold. 2026-09-06: +1 for `./nuxt-module`, which Nuxt loads by specifier from `modules: []` and so cannot live behind an existing entry. +1 for `./annotate`, which is separate so a build plugin does not drag `ts-morph` into a project.

adapterOptions.why: Members of `PreviewAdapterOptions`: what every adapter takes. The single most-read type in the package. 2026-09-06: +2, `delivery` and `assetPath` — one concept, but the second is the path both halves must agree on, and folding it into the first would hide that.

inlineOptions.why: Members of `InlineScriptConfig`: what the generated script carries. Most of them travel in the positional wire tuple, which is append-only.

diagnosticCodes.why: LP codes. A code is a promise to explain one situation; forty is a table someone can skim, and a hundred would be a table nobody reads. 2026-09-06: +1 for LP0409, the strict sanitizer reporting an attribute the 1.x default kept — the one 2.0 behaviour change an upgrading project could otherwise only discover by looking.

sourceModules.why: Source modules in the architecture graph. Files stay under 500 lines, so this is the other half of that rule: many small files are only better than few large ones while the count itself stays legible. 2026-09-06: +2, the Nuxt module and the Next.js config wrapper; +2, the shared runtime-asset descriptor and the Next.js asset route; +2, the SvelteKit and Nuxt ones; +2, the annotator plugin and its entry; +1, the sanitizer's upgrade report; +1, the quarantine for the deprecated 1.x names.

payload-live-preview.api.md.why: The root barrel: the client, the generator, the renderers, the DSL and the plugin surface in one import. The largest number here on purpose — and the one to watch, because every entry below re-exports from it.

payload-live-preview--core.api.md.why: The runtime without the generator and the built-in plugins.

payload-live-preview--server.api.md.why: Everything a server decides with: authorization, tokens, document reads, gated bindings, and reading a verdict back off locals.

payload-live-preview--client.api.md.why: `LivePreviewClient` and what its options and events name.

payload-live-preview--plugins.api.md.why: The manager, the contract and the built-in plugins.

payload-live-preview--fragment.api.md.why: The browser half of the fragment and route strategies.

payload-live-preview--structural.api.md.why: The keyed morph and the structural array renderer.

payload-live-preview--codegen.api.md.why: Type generation and the annotate surface, including the schema shape the annotator reads.

payload-live-preview--astro.api.md.why: The integration, the middleware, the fragment endpoint, and the two 1.x names this entry exported before the 2.0 rename.

payload-live-preview--nextjs.api.md.why: The middleware, the script props, the fragment endpoint, `withLivePreview()` for next.config.ts, and the runtime asset route.

payload-live-preview--lexical.api.md.why: The Lexical renderer and its node registry.

payload-live-preview--nuxt.api.md.why: The Nitro plugin, the handler, the fragment endpoint and the runtime asset route.

payload-live-preview--doctor.api.md.why: `runDoctor()` and the probe analysis as a library.

payload-live-preview--sveltekit.api.md.why: The handle, the fragment endpoint and the runtime asset route.

payload-live-preview--annotate.api.md.why: The build-time annotator: the plugin, the transform behind it, and the schema shape it reads. No ts-morph, which is why it is not part of `./codegen`.

payload-live-preview--nuxt-module.api.md.why: The Nuxt module and the shapes it duck-types off Nuxt, so the package does not depend on `nuxt` to adapt it.

payload-live-preview--vue.api.md.why: The composable, its options and the four refs it returns.

payload-live-preview--react.api.md.why: The hook, its options and the snapshot it returns.

payload-live-preview--codegen--astro.api.why: The Astro integration that runs type generation on start and in dev.

payload-live-preview--lean.api.md.why: The lean runtime artifact as a value, and the type that describes one.

payload-live-preview--astro--middleware-.why: The entry the Astro integration registers as middleware; it reads its options from a virtual module.
